title: Nicotine Patch Therapy in Long COVID: A Quality Assurance Survey
content: Transdermal nicotine has been proposed for long COVID, but evidence is limited and patient feedback in our long COVID specialist clinic has been mixed. We conducted a quality assurance survey to define our position on recommending nicotine patches. A REDCap survey was sent to the Clinic Nineteen patient mailing list between 2023 and 2026 and analysed descriptively. Of 101 respondents who had used nicotine patches, 41 (41%) reported no improvement or worsening, 33 (33%) slight improvement and 27 (27%) decided or vast improvement. Among those who reported overall improvement and rated symptom domains, 51 of 58 (88%) reported at least slight improvement in fatigue and post-exertional malaise and 39 of 51 (76%) in brain fog, whereas sleep, gastrointestinal symptoms, pain and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome changed little. Side effects were none or mild in 63 (62%) and outweighed benefit in 18 (18%). The most common reasons for stopping were no benefit (32 of 59) and side effects (30 of 59). Nicotine patches gave a decided improvement in about a quarter of respondents, mainly in fatigue and cognition, but many had no benefit or intolerable side effects. These data support a carefully monitored trial of nicotine patches for selected patients while controlled trials are awaited.
